name: Hawker 800 / 850 / 900
summary: Midsize descendant of the 1960s de Havilland/Hawker Siddeley HS.125, built in large numbers in the UK and later the US.

wings: Low wing with moderate sweep and noticeable dihedral
Winglets on the 850XP and 900XP; plain tips on most 800s
engines: Two Honeywell TFE731 turbofans in pods on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Fuselage with a row of small oval windows
Large belly fairing (ventral fuel tank) under the wing center section
tail: Horizontal stabilizer mounted partway up the fin (cruciform), not on top
Fin with a long dorsal fillet

tellTales: Small oval windows on a midsize twinjet with a mid-fin tailplane
Bulging belly fairing under the wing
Wing with visible dihedral and moderate sweep

confusedWith.howToTell: The Hawker 800 is smaller with oval windows and a belly fairing; the Falcon 2000 is wider with rounded-rectangle windows.
The Hawker 800 has its tailplane partway up the fin and oval windows; the Beechjet/Hawker 400 is smaller with a T-tail.
The Hawker 800 has a swept wing and mid-fin tailplane; the Excel has a straight wing and a tailplane low on the tail cone.
The Hawker 800 has two engines; the Falcon 50/900 has a third engine intake at the fin root.
The Falcon 20 has small round windows and a low-set tailplane; the Hawker 800 has larger oval windows and a cruciform tail with a long dorsal fillet.
